attributes.rationale: lets an agent prompt a logged-in chatbot web UI like an API call, without an API key or per-token billing
login-gated: MS SSO wall blocks unattended use
login-gated: signup paywall blocks unattended use
simple substring match on the URL so callers can pass loose site names
lets a caller pick a specific underlying model (e.g. Opus vs Haiku) before prompting
talks to local PinchTab daemon at /tabs, /tab, /tabs/<id>/{evaluate,navigate,action}
polls a per-site CSS selector until the composer exists; absence is the login-check failure signal
composer implementation varies by site (ProseMirror/Quill/tiptap, Lexical, native textarea), so injection must vary too
focus, execCommand selectAll+delete, then insertText

execCommand('delete') no-ops on Lexical editors, so select all via DOM Range + insertText instead; Kimi's editor also starts contenteditable=false and needs a real click, wrapped in an 8-attempt retry loop
uses React's native HTMLTextAreaElement value setter + synthetic input event to bypass React's controlled-input tracking
clicks send button where available and enabled, else dispatches synthetic Enter keydown/keypress/keyup
load-bearing reliability trick: Chrome throttles background tabs which stalls streamed SSE responses mid-sentence, so gptbrowser calls POST /tab {action: focus} on every single poll during generation

polls assistant message innerText length plus a generating signal; done = length stable for N consecutive polls and not actively generating. Defaults: poll every 700ms, 6 stable polls (~4.2s), 45s first-token wait, 240s hard ceiling
returns clean innerText with no HTML or markdown fencing artifacts beyond what the site itself renders
installs binary to /opt/homebrew/bin/gptbrowser (not ~/.cargo/bin) so non-interactive shells and sub-agents find it on PATH
isolates the cost difference between shelling out to gptbrowser (one tool call, one string back) versus a sub-agent driving PinchTab directly
both arms used identical Sonnet sub-agent and identical prompt; both arms passed, so this is a cost-per-answer comparison, not a success-rate comparison
gptbrowser arm averages ~51.3k tokens, 1 tool call, ~21s end-to-end vs direct-PinchTab's 7-11 tool calls and 61-199s

both arms pay a fixed ~51.3k token floor (system prompt + tool schemas); marginal cost is ~50 tokens for gptbrowser vs ~5,500 for direct PinchTab, a 10-50x difference, driven largely by direct PinchTab re-reading the growing response text into context on every poll
route 'ask a chatbot web UI something and get text back' tasks through gptbrowser rather than raw browser automation, especially for fan-out sub-agent workflows
splits $ARGUMENTS into URL and PROMPT, runs exactly one Bash call, returns only stdout, reports stderr verbatim on failure, and forbids opening a browser itself

the shipped command's docs still mention only ChatGPT/Gemini/Kimi/DeepSeek while main.rs's Site enum actually supports nine sites including Claude, Perplexity, and z.ai (working) plus Copilot/Grok (pending login)
scopes the slash command to only ever shell out to gptbrowser so it can't be used to smuggle in arbitrary Bash
spin up a sub-agent via the Agent tool and hand it a single gptbrowser call as its entire task rather than letting it drive a browser itself; good fit for parallel fan-out across sites
the binary is Claude-agnostic; any shell/CI step that can run an arbitrary binary can call gptbrowser directly
gives a stable parseable {model,url,prompt,response,elapsed_ms} shape for scripting

runs gptbrowser --json [--model][--timeout] <url> <prompt> and returns response text; isError:true with parsed stderr on non-zero exit
runs gptbrowser --list-models <url> and returns newline-separated available models
overrides the CLI binary location when gptbrowser isn't on $PATH for the environment Claude Code launches from
arguments passed via execFile with an argument array, never shell string interpolation, so prompts with quotes/newlines/special chars are safe
defaults to 300s regardless of timeout_sec; extended to timeout_sec+30s when that's larger, giving gptbrowser's 10-60s runtime headroom
